first.text: Stop there. Let me see your hand.
She looks at the ember a long moment. Her jaw works like she's chewing something bitter.
Mara Tollen. Harbormaster. These days that means I count what's left and try not to count what isn't.
If you're what the old songs say, you picked a fine time to wash up.

choice.text: What happened here?
"What isn't" — who's missing?
Someone in the net-lofts saw Dunstan leave.
How do we push the fog back?
Where do I find the Keeper?
Listen to this. It hums.
Pell has the humming pebble now.
The beacon needs a memory. It could be yours — of Dunstan.
Your gull. The beacon didn't need it.
Aldous says the ferry might run again.
Show Mara the Keeper's sleeve-ember.
The ferry's in.
About Pell and the ferry.
I'll be going.

what_happened.text: Three months back the Hearthspire went dark. The Snuffing, folk call it, like naming it makes it smaller.
The fog came in behind it. First the net-lofts. Then the smokehouse. People go in to fetch a net and come out not knowing whose net it is.

dunstan.text: My brother. Dunstan. Two weeks ago he walked north into the grey with a lantern and no reason he'd give me.
He's not dead. I'd know. I'd— I think I'd know.

beacon_offer.text: The Gull's Beacon, up on the headland. Every midwinter the Keepers lit it from the Spire, and the fog kept its distance.
There's a Keeper in the village. Brother Aldous. Came off the Spire the night it went out and hasn't been sober since.

choice.text: I'll talk to him.
Why haven't you asked him yourself?

why_not.text: I have. He cries. Maybe he'll talk to someone with fire in their hand.

token.text: Take this. It'll get you past the lads at the net-lofts when the time comes.

where_aldous.text: West side, by the Wrens' old house. Follow the smell of cheap spirits.

pebble_kept.text: When the hum reaches her, Mara's eyes go wet. She hums three notes along with it, stops, frowns.
I knew the rest of that. Yesterday I knew it. Keep it safe, Wakebearer.

pebble_given.text: Pell showed me. Carries it everywhere and hums along all day now. Wrong, mind you, but hums it.
Good of you. That child's got precious little that's their own.

dunstan_chose.text: Hesk? Hesk's been Hushed a month. She doesn't know her own—
You tell her: the lantern, the laughing, coming back for his name.
…That's him. That's exactly him, the great fool.
So the fog didn't take him. He went. He walked in there on purpose and didn't tell me why.
I don't know if that's better. Ask me when I've slept.

offer_gull.text: You're asking me to forget my brother.
…He chose, didn't he. Walked off laughing and left me the counting. Maybe I get a choice too.
He's out there. If I forget him, who's left to be waiting when he comes back?

choice.text: Only if you're willing. It has to be your choice.
Forget I asked.

offer_gull_yes.text: She takes something from her coat: a thumb-sized gull whittled from driftwood, its beak worn smooth by a thumb.
He made it for me when I was six and he was ten. Wouldn't let me on the boats, so he brought me a bird.
She walks to the boardwalk gate and holds the gull out into the grey. She stays there a long time. When she comes back the wood is warm, and her eyes are wet and angry.
There. It's all in there. Don't— don't tell me if you use it. I won't know what you mean anyway.

gull_back.text: Mara turns the gull over in her fingers. The warmth fades out of it as you watch, back into her.
Great fool of a bird. Great fool of a brother.
Thank you. I mean it. Now go away before I say something soft.

beacon_lit.text: I watched it catch from the harbor wall. Half the village did. Old Brenner dropped his pipe in the water.
The fog's back past the wall. We can reach the smokehouse again. The lofts, even. You've fed us for the winter, Wakebearer.

lit_pebble.text: She hums, absently — three notes, four — and stops. She frowns at the air.
Was I humming? Odd. I don't know any songs. Never had the voice for it.

lit_knot.text: Strange thing. I went to show Tam how to start a new net and my hands didn't know where to begin. Started from the middle. Works fine.
Suppose that's what it cost. A beginning. We'll manage without one.

lit_gull.text: She glances at the empty stool beside her door, the one with a big man's dent worn into the seat, and looks away without seeing it.
Just me here. Tollens end with me, always have. Never minded.
…Though I keep setting out two cups. Habit, I suppose. Whose, I couldn't tell you.

ferry.text: Does he. Well. He's not wrong, for once.
He told you something, then. You've the look of someone carrying a Keeper's secret. Don't hand it to me; I've enough to carry.
The Tidewright ferry puts in at our dock when it can see us. It hasn't since the Snuffing. No ferryman sails into what they can't see, and I don't blame them.
Now there's a light on the Gull, they'll see it from the lanes. I'll hang the green lantern on the post outside my door. Old harbor signal: passengers waiting.
When they come, you'll hear the horn. Might be days. Might be longer. The sea doesn't hurry for anyone, even you.

sleeve_ember.text: Mara turns the scrap of robe to the light. The stitched ember on it has faded almost to pink.
That's off a Keeper's sleeve. They're buried in those robes, sleeves and all. He cut it off himself?
Then whatever he told you, he meant it. First thing Aldous Wren's meant since he washed up here.
Keep it out of sight on the ferry. Tidewrights don't love Keepers. They'll say the Spire went dark on the Keepers' watch, and they won't be wrong.

farewell.text: Heard it. Whole village heard it. Hesk'll have heard it up in the lofts, if she hears anything now.
Funny thing. I set out two cups this morning, same as always, and I thought: one of those is for a traveller. That'll be you, then. Drink it before you go. It's cold.
There's a tune I've been after all morning. Something to send a boat off with. Can't find it. Never mind; the horn'll do.
Tidewrights'll give you grief about the knot. Let them. The nets still hold. That's what nets are for.

farewell_dunstan.text: And— if you see a big man out there in the fog. Tollen shoulders. Laughs like a dropped anchor.
Tell him the stool's still by the door. Don't tell him to come home. He knows where it is.

farewell_end.text: Go on, then. Light the next one. And eat something before you board; Tidewright cooking is a punishment.

pell_ferry.text: Pell's told me nothing, which is how I know something's up. That bundle's got my good cup in it.
You promised a child a crossing into the fog. Without asking me.
The kid gave up that pebble for this village. Doesn't even know what they gave. Maybe that's earned a bit of sea.

choice.text: I'll keep Pell close. You have my word, on the ember.
You're right. Pell should stay with you.

pell_ferry_yes.text: Mara looks down the dock for a long while. Pell is pretending very hard not to watch.
Pell's not mine to keep. Never was. Nobody I love ever is, it seems.
…Odd. I feel I've said that before, about someone. Can't think who.
Go on, tell the kid before I change my mind. And you bring them back with all their fingers.

pell_ferry_no.text: Then you tell the kid. You made the promise. You unmake it.
She says it without heat, and it lands harder for that.
